subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should stored per-session `/exec` fields be allowed to override later stricter global or per-agent exec security configuration after a Discord session resumes?
rationale: Current docs and tests intentionally support persistent session defaults, but the reported behavior can shadow an operator's later security policy change, so the desired security boundary and upgrade behavior need maintainer intent.

options.title: Make config the security ceiling
options.body: Clamp or clear stored session exec fields when they would loosen current global or agent exec policy, and add migration/reset coverage for existing entries.

options.title: Keep session persistence as-is
options.body: Document that `/exec` session defaults survive config changes and require session reset or tool-deny policy when operators need immediate enforcement.

options.title: Ship explicit reset first
options.body: Add an operator-facing session exec reset or doctor repair path before changing precedence for existing sessions.

recommendation.title: Make config the security ceiling
recommendation.body: Clamp or clear stored session exec fields when they would loosen current global or agent exec policy, and add migration/reset coverage for existing entries.

likelyOwner.reason: The clearest feature-history trail for `/exec` session override semantics and tests points to `steipete`.
